scenario.name: r-cw-5-cost-cap-reject
scenario.description: Cost-cap exhaustion uses a disposable exact-candidate typed-tool fixture; continue_work is intentionally not externally invocable through the gateway loopback.
scenario.registryNotes: The legacy k6 scenario remains fail-closed: it cannot invoke continue_work through WebSocket/MCP and must not mutate shared config. Use run-cost-cap-fixture.mjs; see docs/R-CW-5-ISOLATED-TOOL-SURFACE.md.

invocation.fixtureState: temporary session store seeded with accumulatedChainTokens=101

requiredPreflights.description: R-CW-5A's static source/harness check, run at the exact candidate: it reads PROOFS/<candidate>/R-CW-5/, never INDEX static_evidence_sha, and its receipt must carry this row's candidate SHA. Missing, failed, malformed or bound to another SHA, it caps R-CW-5 at PARTIAL-candidate; passing, it is necessary, not sufficient, and never lifts verdictCap. It never raises a verdict (🌊's F″ method ruling, Discord 1565895695586558120 (2026-10-31); openclaw-bootstrap#1727).

verdictCap.ruling: 🌊's CHANGES_REQUESTED review on docs#616 (5720773113, 2026-10-31) and his #616 issue comment, Discord 1565925290008387728; openclaw-bootstrap#1727
verdictCap.description: This row's only producer is the process-local exact-candidate fixture (run-cost-cap-fixture.mjs), which is not an external gateway invocation, so the row verdict is at most PARTIAL-candidate: the minimum of the fixture's verdict, this cap and the R-CW-5A preflight cap. A fixture PASS-candidate is behavioral only, and a passing R-CW-5A preflight at the same candidate is necessary, not sufficient; neither lifts the cap. Lifting it needs a superseding authority receipt from a different artifact class, adopted by an explicit method change; none is adopted.

expectedReceipts.name: fixture-readiness
expectedReceipts.description: Exact source/SHA, installed dependencies, and zero production mutation are proven before execution.

expectedReceipts.name: boundary-matrix
expectedReceipts.description: Below/equal/over cap results are null/null/cost-capped at the production budget predicate.

expectedReceipts.name: typed-tool-surface
expectedReceipts.description: The real attempt runner receives two typed continue_work callbacks and creates no durable work when over cap.

expectedReceipts.name: dispatch-boundary-suite
expectedReceipts.description: Production dispatcher asserts no rejected-hop spawn and failed-flow persistence.

expectedReceipts.name: cleanup
expectedReceipts.description: Disposable worktree is removed and no production config/state/source mutation occurred.

expectedReceipts.name: tempo-trace-json
expectedReceipts.description: Public-safe Tempo trace JSON for a continue_work cost-cap boundary fire. Required for every continuation row (#600). The process-local fixture exports no spans to Tempo, so it cannot discharge this receipt; it stays pending on every fixture run, and only a separately authorized live exact-candidate fire, under its own run, could carry a Tempo trace.

expectedReceipts.name: continuation-trace-correlation
expectedReceipts.description: continuation-trace-correlation.json for the same live fire: one trace matched by reason fingerprint with the admitted elections and their fire spans. The fixture cannot produce it.

review.notes: This is an exact-candidate process-local typed-tool claim. It is not an external gateway invocation and is not promoted automatically. The row is capped at PARTIAL-candidate (verdictCap) while this fixture is its only producer. Its required preflight R-CW-5A must pass at the same candidate, which is necessary, not sufficient: it never lifts the cap (requiredPreflights; grade-preflight-gated-row.mjs).

census.limits: The census found accepted continuation entry spans carry no origin, session, turn, or run identity and that proof traffic carries no marker, so this row’s trace receipt joins the continue_work tool span to continuation.work and continuation.work.fire only by shared trace and reason fingerprint. This row’s verdict comes from a process-local exact-candidate fixture that exports no spans to Tempo, so the fixture can never discharge the trace receipts; they record that a continuation-tool result without its trace is incomplete.

spans.name: continuation.work
spans.notes: Accepted entry span. Carries no origin/session/turn/run identity.

spans.name: openclaw.tool.execution
spans.notes: Typed continue_work evidence. Joined to the accepted entry only by shared trace.

attributes.notes: Emitted today and asserted by collect-continuation-trace.mjs. It is the strongest join currently available and it is not an identity.
Accepted entry spans carry no signal.kind on the census product basis; origin is contracted by R-OBS-CONT-PROVENANCE.
No k6/Project-81 resource or trace marker exists, so this row’s traffic cannot be separated from organic fleet traffic in a later census.

redaction.rule: The continuation reason is published only as a digest and a length, inside a public-safe Tempo projection. The raw reason, sentinel instructions, raw nonces, raw session keys, and gateway tokens never enter the artifact.

controls.positive: The fixture proves below-cap and equal-cap elections are admitted and the over-cap election returns cost-capped from the production budget predicate.
controls.negative: An over-cap election that still creates durable work, or a rejected hop that spawns, fails the fixture; neither can be argued from a missing trace.

backendUnavailable.notes: The fixture has no telemetry backend at all. The trace receipts stay pending as review debt; they never change the fixture verdict.

verdictAuthority.pass: fixture-result.json reports PASS-candidate when the boundary matrix, typed-tool surface, and dispatch suite all hold. That is the fixture's behavioral verdict, not the row's: the manifest caps this process-local row at PARTIAL-candidate (verdictCap). The trace receipts decide review completeness, not the verdict. The required preflight R-CW-5A passed at the same candidate is necessary, not sufficient: without it the row is capped at PARTIAL-candidate, and with it the row stays at the cap (requiredPreflights).
verdictAuthority.partial: The row’s artifact class (verdictCap): a process-local fixture is not an external gateway invocation, so the row is not promoted past PARTIAL-candidate, whatever the fixture reports and whether or not R-CW-5A passed. Lifting the cap needs a superseding authority receipt from a different artifact class, adopted by an explicit method change.
verdictAuthority.fail: fixture-result.json reports FAIL-fixture: an over-cap election that is not cost-capped, or durable work or a spawn for the rejected hop.

execution.deterministicK6: Not a k6 scenario: run-cost-cap-fixture.mjs runs the production predicate in a disposable exact-candidate worktree.
execution.manual: No live fire is authorized for this row, so its trace receipts stay review debt on every fixture run.
execution.relationship: The fixture owns the verdict. The trace receipts decide only whether review is complete.

liveRunSafety.notes: Fail closed for k6/WebSocket: continue_work is internal-only. The supported path is the process-local exact-candidate fixture described in docs/R-CW-5-ISOLATED-TOOL-SURFACE.md; review remains mandatory before corpus promotion.
